info.desc: "Weezer" may refer to: the May 1994 Blue Album (seen here) the May 2001 Green Album the June 2008 Red Album the April 2016 White Album the January 2019 Teal Album the March 2019 Black Album Weezer is the debut studio album by American rock band Weezer, released on May 10, 1994, by DGC Records. It was produced by Ric Ocasek. Weezer formed in Los Angeles in 1992, and initially struggled to engage audiences, who were more interested in grunge. Weezer (Green Album) , Weezer (Red Album), and Weezer (Deluxe Edition) were all renamed to "Weezer" in February 2023. .

podcast.body: Referred to as "the blue one," this debut album features the song "My Name Is Jonas" and is an early showcase of Weezer's embrace of their geekiness, which they continued to celebrate in their subsequent work. "Weezer from their debut album, which is the blue one, and my name is Jonas."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Released in 1994, Weezer's debut album, commonly known as the "Blue Album," went on to sell over 15 million copies. Its success was significantly bolstered by songs like "Buddy Holly," which, despite initial reluctance from Rivers Cuomo, was included after persuasion from producer Ric Ocasek and the rest of the band. "And that debut blue album would later go on to sell somewhere north of 15 million copies."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Released in 1994, this album by the Los Angeles band Weezer is described as "kind of second wave emo." The band, particularly singer Rivers Cuomo, was characterized by nerdy and geeky aesthetics and highly confessional lyrics exploring fear, bitterness, and confusion, often accompanied by big, loud guitars with punk rock influences. "Weezer from their blue album, kind of second wave emo."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Released on May 10th, 1994, this debut album was recorded at Jimmy Hendrix's Electric Lady Studio in New York for about six weeks starting in August 1993. It sold over 15 million copies worldwide and gained additional revenue from appearances in video games. The band lineup changed during recording as guitarist Jason Cropper departed. "The blue album started to sell and sell and sell."

podcast.body: This album features the "proper version" of "Undone the Sweater Song," which sounded different in its earlier demo stages. "The proper version is on the blue album, but before it got that far, it sounded like that."

podcast.body: Weezer's debut album, commonly known as the "Blue Album," was a significant success that prompted Rivers Cuomo's ambitious plans for their second record. Its "big debut" established the band and set high expectations for follow-up material. "After the big debut of the Blue Album, Rivers Cuomo wanted the second Weezer record to be a space opera."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Weezer's self-titled debut (known as the Blue Album) was released on May 10, 1994, and defied easy categorization: somewhat grungy but not, nerdy and slacker-ish in a good way, rooted in power pop but with a punk spirit. It was a major critical and commercial success and laid groundwork for emo in the years that followed. Worldwide sales exceeded 15 million copies — a figure many people do not realize. "A lot of people don't realize that Weezer's Blue Album sold at least 15 million copies worldwide."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Released in 2001, this album followed Weezer's 2000 Warped Tour appearance, which served as a way for the band to ease back into performing after a hiatus during which Rivers Cuomo attended Harvard. "just before the Green album in 2001."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: The release of this album in 2001 marked a significant turning point, effectively kickstarting the "Weezer we know today." It featured a lineup change with Mikey Welsh replaced by Scott Schreiner due to Welsh's severe mental health issues and drug use, leading to his hospitalization. "The Weezer we know today really began in 2001 when they released their third record, the one known as the Green Album for obvious reasons."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This album featured the single "Pork and Beans", known for its video which incorporated various internet personalities and memes of the day. The band's leader, Rivers Cuomo, with his bookish, neurotic, and socially awkward personality, reinforces Weezer's image as a quintessential nerd rock band. "If you remember the video, if you're doing all the internet personalities and memes of the day, it's really tough to imagine anything more nerdy."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This album features the song "Troublemaker," which was used in an Apple iPhone advertising campaign in 2009. "Weezer and troublemaker from the Red Album, one of dozens and dozens and dozens of songs used by Apple in their TV commercials."

podcast.body: This was the band's sixth album, following the Blue Album (1994) and Green Album (2001). It was self-titled and simply known as the Red Album due to its color. The album marked the beginning of a very prolific period for the band and included an interview with the host incorporated into the liner notes. "The red album marked the beginning of a very prolific period for the band."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Weezer's tenth album, released on April Fool's Day 2016, marked a return to using colors for album titles. Following the mixed commercial success of "Everything Will Be All Right in the End," the band decided to experiment again. It featured a new producer, Jack Sinclair, a longtime Weezer fan who also fronted a tribute band called Wannabeezer, and who possessed deep insights into the band's sound. "Weezer's 10th album went back to using colors."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.body: This album was released digitally in January 2019 without warning, consisting entirely of cover songs. Rivers Cuomo used a computer program that analyzed Spotify data to identify popular songs not tagged as Alt Rock or Classic Rock, released before 1994, to select the tracks. The band aimed to play the top 10 songs as accurately as possible, with TLC's "No Scrubs" being the only exception to the 1994 rule because "it was just cool." "The Teal album, and it showed up in January 2019 with no warning whatsoever."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Rivers Cuomo and Weezer - Alt-Rock's Nerd Heroes Part 2

podcast.body: This was officially Studio Album No. 15, released after the Teal Album's two-month run. Its release was preceded by a clever internet marketing campaign: a Yelp profile appeared on October 9, 2018, shared by the official Weezer Twitter account, with reviews containing mysterious lyrics from the new album, all about places with "Black" in their name. A new song featuring these lyrics, "Can't Knock the Hustle," was released two days later. "Once the Teele album had its run, which was all two months, it was finally time for the Black Album."
